title: "Feature"
description: "An input variable or measurable property used by a model to make predictions."

difficulty: "Beginner"

## Simple explanation

A feature is a piece of information supplied to a model about an example.
For a house-price model, features might include floor area, location, and
number of bedrooms.

## Technical explanation

Features are represented as input variables, often organized into a
vector or tensor $x$. Features may be raw observations, transformed
values, learned representations, or metadata. Their definition and
availability must be consistent across training and inference.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Feature quality, correctness, and availability strongly affect model
behaviour. Feature definitions also influence data pipelines,
interpretability, privacy, and the risk of leakage.

## How it works

An application collects or derives feature values, validates them, and
passes them to a model in the expected representation. A model uses
learned parameters to combine features into predictions.

## Practical example

For image classification, the pixels or a transformed tensor of pixel
values are model inputs. In a tabular model, age or transaction amount
may be individual features.

## Common misconceptions

- A feature is not necessarily a human-interpretable concept.
- More features do not automatically improve a model.
- Features derived using information unavailable at prediction time can
  cause data leakage.
